whyItMatters: ECS task launches become much more important when the task activates a role with material privilege. The security value comes from the resolved task role and its permissions, not from how the task or role is named.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may use RunTask to execute a workload under a powerful task role and then access secrets, assume roles, or modify cloud control-plane resources.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: Short-lived ECS tasks are attractive because they blend into ordinary operations while still providing controlled code execution and role credentials.
threatContext.whyItMatters: The strongest signal is what the task role can do after launch, not whether the task family contains words like admin.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, a single ad hoc task run can silently activate broad permissions through a neutrally named task definition or overridden role.

requiredLogSources: AWS CloudTrail management events for ECS
loggingRequirements: RunTask telemetry must be ingested with overrides preserved.
The platform should resolve taskRoleArn and executionRoleArn from the task definition.
Task-role permissions should be semantically classified before alerting at high severity.
limitations: The raw RunTask event usually does not contain the fully resolved role without ECS task-definition lookups.
Name-based matching is unreliable for both task definitions and roles.
Some privileged task roles are legitimate in tightly controlled service environments.

rawToNormalized.notes: Final resolved task role used by the task
Semantic privilege class of the resolved task role

enrichment.description: Classify the final task role as admin-equivalent, role-chaining, secrets-accessing, pass-role capable, or lower risk.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Captures real privilege even when names are neutral.

enrichment.dimension: Execution Role vs Task Role Split
enrichment.description: Distinguish image-pull and logging permissions from application permissions available to the container.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Prevents over-alerting on benign execution roles while highlighting application-role risk.

enrichment.description: Determine whether the cluster, task family, and role pairing is normal for the environment.
examples: prod cluster with ad hoc ops task
unexpected task role on customer-facing service
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Separates service design from suspicious workload activation.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This rule should resolve the task's final task role, whether from the task definition or a runtime override, then classify that role semantically. The detection becomes high value when the task role grants material privilege such as role chaining, secrets access, or broad administration.
conditions: resolved task role is classified as admin-equivalent, role-chaining, secrets-accessing, pass-role capable, or otherwise high-risk
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Resolve the final task role before evaluating risk. 2. Do not depend on task-definition or role-name substrings. 3. Escalate when the actor is unexpected or the task uses runtime overrides.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire when RunTask activates a task role whose effective permissions materially expand what the workload can do.

quality.falsePositiveRate: Low-Medium with resolved role classification; high with name heuristics

whereItRuns: Athena with ECS and IAM inventory
deployment.scheduling: Real-time is useful because the task role can be used immediately after launch.
considerations: This is the permission-aware companion to `det-070`.
Task-definition and role resolution are mandatory dependencies.
